stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: Let $p:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of schemes. Write $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}=(\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{d}\Omega^1_{X/S}\xrightarrow{d}\Omega^2_{X/S}\to\cdots)$ for the relative de Rham complex, where $\Omega^i_{X/S}=\bigwedge^i_{\mathcal O_X}\Omega^1_{X/S}$. Then the derived direct image $Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ belongs to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_S)$: every cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^n(Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})$ is quasi-coherent on $S$.
hypotheses: $p:X\to S$ is a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of schemes.
conclusions: For all $n\in\mathbb Z$, $\mathcal H^n(Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})$ is quasi-coherent.

reason: Uses the first-quadrant hypercohomology spectral sequence E1^{a,b}=R^b f_*Omega^a_{X/S} and quasi-coherence of higher direct images for qcqs morphisms. All graded pieces and thus the abutment have quasi-coherent cohomology.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: Let $p:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes, and assume $S$ is locally Noetherian. Let $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ denote the relative de Rham complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, with $\Omega^a_{X/S}=\bigwedge^a_{\mathcal O_X}\Omega^1_{X/S}$ placed in cohomological degree $a$. Then the derived direct image $Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ is an object of $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_S)$: its cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^n(Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})$ are coherent $\mathcal O_S$-modules for all integers $n$.
hypotheses: $p:X\to S$ is proper and $S$ is locally Noetherian.
conclusions: Every cohomology sheaf of $Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ is coherent on $S$.

reason: Invokes coherence of each Omega^i under the proper finite-type morphism over locally Noetherian S, and applies the earlier spectral-sequence argument with the proper-pushforward coherence theorem.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper, smooth morphism of schemes. For $p\geq 0$ put $\Omega^p_{X/S}=\bigwedge^p_{\mathcal O_X}\Omega^1_{X/S}$, and let $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ be the relative de Rham complex. Each $Rf_*\Omega^p_{X/S}$ and the derived direct image $Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ are perfect objects of $D(\mathcal O_S)$.

More precisely, for every morphism $g:S'\to S$ of schemes, let $X'=X\times_S S'$, $g':X'\to X$, and $f':X'\to S'$ be the induced maps. For each $p\geq0$ the canonical derived base-change map
$$Lg^*(Rf_*\Omega^p_{X/S})\longrightarrow Rf'_*\Omega^p_{X'/S'}$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_{S'})$, and so is the analogous map
$$Lg^*(Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})\longrightarrow Rf'_*\Omega^\bullet_{X'/S'}.$$
hypotheses: $f:X\to S$ is proper and smooth; for base change, $S'\to S$ is arbitrary and $X'=X\times_S S'$.
conclusions: The derived pushforwards of every $\Omega^p_{X/S}$ and of the full relative de Rham complex are perfect and satisfy derived base change for every $S'\to S$.

reason: Smoothness makes Omega^p finite locally free and base-change compatible, and proper flat perfect direct-image theory gives perfect pushforwards with derived base change. A finite truncation filtration of the relative de Rham complex, using exact triangles and two-out-of-three for perfect objects and base change, extends this to the entire complex.
